options.name: api_key
options.description: API key of your NetOrca team. The NetOrca API supports API-key authentication only - there is no username/password mode. Treat the key like a password - supply it via the E(NETORCA_API_KEY) environment variable (for example from a CI/CD secret) or from Ansible Vault, never as a literal in a playbook. If not set, the value of the E(NETORCA_API_KEY) environment variable is used.

options.name: api_url
options.description: Base URL of the NetOrca API, for example C(https://api.example.netorca.io). The URL is normalised to end in a single C(/v1), so passing it with or without the suffix both work. If not set, the value of the E(NETORCA_API_URL) environment variable is used.

options.name: context
options.description: Point of view for the request. The same query returns different data depending on which side of the service relationship your team is on. V(serviceowner) operates on the services your team I(offers) - the requests made against them, their service items and deployed items. This is the side that validates, approves, deploys and completes changes. options.name: id
options.description: Return only the pack data record with this ID. If the ID does not exist, an empty list is returned.

options.name: limit
options.description: Maximum number of results to return. Results are auto-paginated, so by default all matching records are returned regardless of the API's page size.

options.name: object_id
options.description: Together with O(stage), return the newest record of that stage for this service item (or service). Returns an empty list when the object has no data for the stage yet.

options.name: ordering
options.description: Server-side field to order results by, for example V(created) or V(modified). Prefix with C(-) for descending order - V(-modified) returns the most recently changed records first.

options.name: stage
options.description: The pipeline stage whose newest data the staged lookup returns.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Whether to validate TLS certificates when talking to the API. Only disable this for lab instances with self-signed certificates. If not set, the value of the E(NETORCA_VALIDATE_CERTS) environment variable is used.
